title: Ambient inverse of a comparison, zero off its invertible locus
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with zero morphisms, $X,Y\in\mathcal C$ and $a:X\to Y$. Define $\operatorname{inverseOrZero}(a):Y\to X$ to be the uniquely determined inverse $a^{-1}$ when $a$ is an isomorphism, and the zero morphism otherwise. The choice of branch uses classical decidability of the proposition that $a$ is an isomorphism. This is an ambient total definition for writing normalized completion comparisons; on their specified invertible domains it is precisely the usual inverse. It does not assert that any comparison is invertible.
